title: 36 questions people ask about AI visibility
source: Periodic Table of AI Visibility, edition 2026.2

questions.q: Why doesn't ChatGPT mention my company?
questions.s: Your buyer asked, got three names, and you weren't one of them. Each engine chooses differently, and you only know you're missing from the ones you checked.

questions.q: Google's AI Overview shows my competitors, not me.
questions.s: The answer box took the click that used to be yours. Position one doesn't matter if the box above it names someone else.

questions.q: How do I show up in Perplexity or Grok?
questions.s: Different engines read different things: Perplexity reads the open web, Grok reads live posts, Gemini reads inside Workspace. One fix doesn't cover all eight.

questions.q: Is my website blocked from ChatGPT?
questions.s: One line in robots.txt meant for scrapers can block the crawler that feeds the answer, and your analytics will never tell you.

questions.q: How do I know if AI crawlers can even read my site?
questions.s: If there's no sitemap entry and nothing links to a page, no engine finds it. Existing is not the same as being found.

questions.q: What is llms.txt and do I need it?
questions.s: It's a note taped to the front door for robots. Cheap to make; Google says it ignores it. Worth an hour, not a week.

questions.q: Why does AI quote my competitor's page and not mine?
questions.s: Same claim, same product, theirs gets picked. Usually the page the engine could actually read: rendered on the server, question-shaped headings, each section standing on its own.

questions.q: ChatGPT gives outdated information about my product.
questions.s: The old page won. Three copies with no canonical, or no honest updated date, and the engine picks the stale one.

questions.q: My videos and screenshots never show up in AI answers.
questions.s: Because there are no words in them. A video with no transcript page and a chart whose alt text says 'chart.png' are blank to retrieval.

parts.group: Signals, part 1 — what the sentence says

questions.q: ChatGPT describes my product wrong.
questions.s: Your first line says 'we empower modern teams.' The model had to guess what you do, and it guessed from someone else's page.

questions.q: AI won't repeat my claims or my numbers.
questions.s: 'Fast onboarding' can't be quoted. 'Live in 4 days for teams under 50' can. No number, no source, no citation.

questions.q: When someone asks AI to compare me to a competitor, I lose.
questions.s: Because you never wrote the comparison. The review site with ads did, and the engine cited them.

parts.group: Signals, part 2 — what the page offers

questions.q: AI lists my competitors with prices and leaves me out.
questions.s: 'Contact us for pricing' removed you from every 'how much does it cost' answer. A starting price puts you back in.

questions.q: AI answers questions about my product from a review site's FAQ instead of mine.
questions.s: Your support tickets already hold the real questions. Ten of them, answered in two sentences each, get lifted word for word.

questions.q: When someone asks 'what is [my category]', AI defines it using a competitor.
questions.s: The definition line at the top of a page is the front door. If yours isn't there, theirs is.

questions.q: What kind of content actually gets cited by AI?
questions.s: Evidence, not opinion. A teardown, a benchmark, a dataset, a measured case study, a runbook. Most B2B sites have none.

questions.q: Why don't my blog posts show up in AI answers?
questions.s: Fifty posts of opinion are fifty pages with nothing attributable. One benchmark with a method and a date beats all of them.

questions.q: AI cites a competitor's study in my category.
questions.s: They published the number. You can publish yours: fifty samples, a stated method, a date. Small is fine.

questions.q: Do videos help with AI visibility?
questions.s: Only with words attached. The video is the trust layer; the transcript is the retrieval layer. You need both.

questions.q: AI never links to my tools or calculators.
questions.s: Because they're gated. The moment a calculator asks for an email, it stops being linked. Ungate the tool, gate the custom result.

questions.q: Does a newsletter or a template help me get cited?
questions.s: They build the audience that later types your name into an engine. Recognition first, citation later.

questions.q: Does posting on LinkedIn help AI visibility?
questions.s: Almost nothing posted there gets cited. It's where you're seen, not where you're cited. Different job.

questions.q: Why does AI cite Reddit over my own website?
questions.s: Because the discussion is real. One honest thread can outrank your whole site, and one sales pitch gets you banned.

questions.q: Does YouTube or GitHub get cited by ChatGPT?
questions.s: YouTube is consistently among the most-cited domains, and a README on GitHub is a document on a trusted domain. Both read closely.

questions.q: Do G2 or Capterra reviews affect AI answers?
questions.s: 'Best X tools' answers lean on review sites. An empty profile reads as an inactive vendor.

questions.q: My AWS Marketplace listing doesn't show up in AI answers.
questions.s: Treated as a form it tells engines nothing. Treated as a landing page, with a definition, proof and a price, it gets cited for 'where can I buy X'.

questions.q: Do guest posts and podcasts help with AI visibility?
questions.s: A transcript page on someone else's trusted domain is a citation you borrowed. No transcript, no retrieval value.

questions.q: How do I track AI visibility?
questions.s: Thirty real buyer questions, frozen, asked monthly. Named in 6 of 30 is 20% share. That's the scoreboard.

questions.q: How do I measure ChatGPT mentions of my brand?
questions.s: Mentions come before citations. Track named-but-unlinked separately; it's the first sign something started working.

questions.q: AI search traffic isn't showing in my analytics.
questions.s: Many AI visits arrive as 'direct.' Segment the ones you can see; they're under 2% of traffic and the highest-intent cohort on the site.

questions.q: My site disappeared from ChatGPT.
questions.s: A 'block all bots' rule meant for scrapers blocked the crawlers that feed the answer. Months invisible, five-minute fix.

questions.q: My pricing page shows up blank to AI.
questions.s: It's built in JavaScript. To most crawlers the page is a header and nothing else. View source and look for your main claim.

questions.q: Does gated content hurt AI visibility?
questions.s: Your best proof behind an email form is invisible to every engine and most buyers. Ungate the proof; gate the tailored thing.

questions.q: Does duplicate content hurt AI search?
questions.s: The same article at three addresses splits authority three ways. None of them wins.

questions.q: Does AI-generated content hurt AI visibility?
questions.s: Fifty thin posts buried the three good ones and taught the engines your name means noise. Deleting is faster than waiting.

questions.q: Do pages without dates get cited?
questions.s: Undated reads as possibly stale, and stale gets skipped on anything time-sensitive. Old but dated beats new but undated.
